overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics indicates that extreme space scenarios, hypothetical 'what-if' planetary drops, and bizarre physical phenomena with strong visual hooks generate the highest views-per-day and engagement rates (likes-per-view). Content featuring space wonders (e.g., TrES-2b, liquid diamond planets, and burning ice worlds) significantly outperforms standard psychological facts and older biological trivia. Recent 7-day uploads are driving almost all momentum, led by high-concept astronomy and cosmic what-if scenarios.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 and 972 views rapidly within their short lifespans with high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on immersive, second-person 'What If' space survival hooks that combine extreme physics with surreal planetary environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) achieved rapid velocity with strong engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form videos focusing on planetary extremes (e.g., weird weather, extreme densities, bizarre light absorption in deep space).

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) and general psychological tricks stagnated below 60 lifetime views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks and brain trivia unless paired with an extreme, counter-intuitive neurological mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts such as octopus hearts or simple longevity trivia yielded low velocity outside of initial bursts compared to high-concept space content.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal-related content into cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric context rather than simple listicle facts.

next_video.hook_style: Second-person visceral survival threat combined with impossible physics
next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Coldest Place in the Universe (The Boomerang Nebula)?
next_video.opening_direction: Instantly place the viewer falling into a cosmic void colder than absolute zero space background, showing instant molecular freeze.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this nebula is actively freezing light itself, trapping your falling shadow in time.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary and space survival format while introducing a brand new celestial object (The Boomerang Nebula) to maintain freshness.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use diamond, glass, iron, ruby, or burning ice planets
Must feature a completely new celestial entity not in past history
Keep pacing under 16 seconds for optimal loop retention

experiment: Test whether framing an astronomy fact as an active second-person survival scenario ('What If You Fell Into...') retains viewers past the 5-second mark better than declarative statement hooks ('This Star Is...').
